title: Gl 229 HARPS sampling gives more than 0.99 squared overlap between 122-day and third-year extraction waves
abstract: We test a possible extraction effect at three reported planet periods for Gl 229. HARPS-RVBank version 02 gives 200 accepted exposures and 197 nightly pairs. The DRS minus SERVAL wave has an amplitude of 0.486 m/s at 122 days. Conditional tests that allow 90-day or 365-day noise blocks do not pass a 0.05 family threshold. After era offsets and quadratic time terms, the squared overlap between the 122-day and 121.75-day wave spaces is 0.9915 to 0.9966. A unit third-year wave gives a fitted 122-day amplitude of 0.993 to 1.004 m/s across 64 phases. Thus this sampling cannot use a small paired difference to assign a unique cause at the fixed 122-day period. The 471-day and 523.2-day differences also lack clear support. This is a sampling and extraction test, not a new planet or a proof of an annual instrument effect. Both products use the same spectra. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, figures and external retrieval steps are included.

display.caption: The 122-day and 121.75-day wave spaces have almost the same shape on the retained nights, after removal of era offsets and quadratic time terms. The right panel shows alternative fits to the same difference values.

Fitted difference amplitudes under four nuisance models, and conditional tail fractions for a three-period maximum. The large BERV control amplitude does not establish a stronger signal; it shows sensitivity to the nuisance model.

citations.reason: The 2025 Gl 229 analysis challenges earlier planet claims. It motivates this paired extraction test.

Shows that Earth motion across detector boundaries can cause annual HARPS signals.
